conclusion: Inference-aligned CE broadly follows playing strength but is not monotonic; none of the learned policies beats raw BT4 on either shared validation pool.
findings: Native BT4 CE is 1.411522 on Hero validation and 1.341258 on sequential validation, the lowest among the seven policies.

HH-002 native CE is 1.443862/1.371600, better than Hero1 native 1.492503/1.423952 but worse than raw BT4. The existing HH-002 native game score against raw is 48.24%, paired 95% interval 36.24%-60.25%; degradation in playing strength remains unestablished.
HH-002 one-pass DFM improves CE on both pools versus old Hero1 one-pass, and wins their direct match with 65.82% score. It still has substantially worse CE and observed BT4 score than native policy.
HH-002 eight-pass DFM worsens both CE and play versus HH-002 one-pass; its direct game score against one-pass is 35.35%, paired 95% interval 23.35%-47.36%.

A direct counterexample to monotonic CE-to-strength ranking: HH-002 eight-pass has higher CE than Hero1 eight-pass on both pools (2.112109 versus 2.073894; 2.036568 versus 2.011983), but wins their direct match with 65.82% score, paired 95% interval 53.82%-77.82%. Its played-move top-1 accuracy is nevertheless higher on both pools (44.64% versus 43.75%; 47.08% versus 45.81%).

Probability loss, argmax move agreement and game outcome are distinct measurements. Calibration, non-optimal played-move labels, distribution shift and rare consequential blunders are possible explanations, not causes isolated by this experiment.
recommendation: Retain full-history raw BT4 as the strength anchor. Track shared inference-aligned legal CE and top-1 for inexpensive screening, but require paired games against BT4 to establish a strength improvement; do not select architectures by composite training loss or CE alone.

execution.accounting_caveat: Workspace meter readings can reconcile with lag and are not isolated experiment invoices; retain full declared reservations for subsequent launch gates.

limits: Reused development validation and opening pools, not a fresh held-out strength test. Played-move labels are not certified optimal. Preserve model-specific history contracts. No new training, games, search, absolute Elo or promotion claim.
